text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Lawyers representing Ovahimba people who oppose the Epupa hydro-electric scheme are to ask the High Court for protection against harassment by the Namibian security forces. Security force members disrupted a meeting between legal advisers and an Ovahimba delegation at the weekend.

- Southern African countries battling to control the spread of deadly cattle lung sickness want to set up a buffer zone between clean and infected areas. A buffer zone has been proposed from the Atlantic ocean across northern Namibia into northern Botswana and western Zambia.

- Safari company Anvo Hunting has challenged a statement by the government that its joint community project with a community at Popa Falls in Western Caprivi is illegal. The company says both Anvo and the community have permission for the project from the ministry of environment and tourism. The local residents are due to be evicted from the project to make way for extensions to a penal centre.
- German-speaking teachers from across the country met at the weekend for their annual education conference.

- Sponsors, organisers and soccer fans were disappointed by the state broadcaster's inability to broadcast live the match between Namibia and Gabon. It ended in a one-all draw, ensuring Namibia's place in the final of the African Nations Cup in Burkina Faso next year.
